sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 2

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 2:1
items.html:
It explains the ten Sefirot of reflected light, and it contains three matters: 1. That the measure of light that was fit to be received in Malchut, had the screen not rejected it backward, is called reflected light. 2. After the restriction, the reflected light became a vessel of reception for the upper light in place of phase four. 3. Since phase four clothed all the phases Keter, Hochma, Bina and ZA before the restriction, five phases of light are therefore discerned in the reflected light that is rejected from it, which clothe the five phases KHB TM of direct light. And in Item 3 it explains the ten Sefirot called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida, and the ten Sefirot called root, Neshama, Guf, garment and hall.

The ten Sefirot of direct light are clothed in the ten Sefirot of reflected light
And the matter of the ten Sefirot of reflected light is what is brought here in the words of the ARI (Chapter 1, Items 1, 2 and 3): that they emerge through the expansion of Ein Sof in the meaning of a coupling by striking upon the screen that is in the vessel of Malchut of direct light. For the screen detains the direct light that belongs to the vessel of Malchut, so that it should not expand within her, and returns it to its place. And this reflected light — that is, the whole of that measure of light which was fit to be received in the vessel of Malchut and which she did not receive, and which was rejected from her backward — is not regarded as having vanished from there; rather, it became a phase of a vessel of reception, for it ascends and clothes all four phases of direct light. Thus there are here two phases of ten Sefirot that clothe one another, for the ten Sefirot of direct light are clothed in the ten Sefirot of reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 2:2
items.html:
The light that was fit to be received in phase four, had the screen not detained it, is called reflected light. After the restriction the reflected light became a vessel of reception in place of phase four, who was restricted.
And although the whole of the reflected light that ascends is nothing but the light of Malchut alone, as has been explained, we nevertheless discern ten Sefirot in this reflected light. And the reason is that Malchut alone was the vessel of reception for all the ten Sefirot before the restriction, for there is nothing whatsoever of the phase of a vessel of reception in the nine Sefirot; rather, they are regarded as light itself, as the ARI writes here (Chapter 12, Item 1, and in Inner Light, ibid., Item 2). And after the restriction, from which time onward Malchut can no longer receive any direct light, that same reflected light which is rejected from Malchut became a phase of a vessel of reception in her place (as written in Inner Observation, Part 2, Sub Header, “And know,” and Sub Header, “Now”). Therefore five phases of vessels are discerned in the light of Malchut from before the restriction, corresponding to each phase of direct light that Malchut clothed there. And now, when the reflected light serves in place of Malchut, we discern in this light that is rejected from Malchut ten Sefirot as well, in which the ten Sefirot of direct light are clothed. And likewise we discern in the vessel of Malchut five phases that are empty of the light belonging to her — that is, of what she had before the restriction.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 2:3
items.html:
An explanation of the ten Sefirot called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida, and those called root, Neshama, Guf, garment and hall
The difference between the ten Sefirot called KHB TM and the ten Sefirot called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida is this: the vessels of the ten Sefirot are called KHB TM, and the lights within them are called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya and Yechida. And the ten Sefirot that are called root, Neshama, Guf, garment and hall have a particular signification — that they lack ZA and Malchut of the vessels, and Haya and Yechida of the lights, and there is in them only KHB of the vessels, which are called root, Neshama and Guf, and Nefesh, Ruach and Neshama of the lights. And this is what came about in the second restriction, through the ascent of Malchut to Bina (as written here in Chapter 10).
